subject.title: Usage/cost attribution is provider-keyed: mixed API+subscription and multi-account setups show wrong billing mode/quota

question: Should OpenClaw make session usage and provider usage summaries credential-keyed now, and should the public shape expose serving authProfileId, credential type, or both?
rationale: The fix changes session projections, provider usage summary shape, and provider/plugin-facing attribution semantics, so automation should not choose the durable data contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Credential-keyed contract
options.body: Record the serving auth profile or stable account key on run/session projections and usage snapshots, then attach quota and billing display to matching credentials across UI and CLI surfaces.

options.title: Credential-type stopgap
options.body: Record only subscription-versus-API-key billing mode for cost display now, while leaving per-account quota attribution for a later contract change.

options.title: Defer until plan-usage PR settles
options.body: Keep this issue open while the linked provider plan-usage PR is reviewed, then decide the attribution contract once the shipped UI surface is clear.

recommendation.title: Credential-keyed contract
recommendation.body: Record the serving auth profile or stable account key on run/session projections and usage snapshots, then attach quota and billing display to matching credentials across UI and CLI surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the current issue, the linked plan-usage PR, and earlier provider-usage history that makes him the best available owner for the product/data-contract choice.
